scope: Broad inventory of genuine, conditional, unverified, non-equivalent and prohibited ways to access or move value from a mainland-China CNY account. A listed candidate is not a recommendation or proof of user eligibility.
source_policy: Regulatory/tax rows cite government sources. Provider-product rows additionally cite the provider's own official page as the primary source for that product; generic marketing is not treated as proof of China-specific eligibility, price or limits. Jurisdiction source IDs resolve through research/china.json and research/us.json.

routes.name: Documented bank salary / current-income conversion and wire
routes.mechanism: Bank verifies lawful RMB income and tax/source evidence, converts CNY to USD and remits to the approved overseas account.
routes.eligibility: Qualifying outside individual with genuine current-account income; classification and bank acceptance must be confirmed.
requirements: Tax evidence where taxable; lawful non-taxable-income explanation where applicable
Overseas recipient/account details accepted by the bank
routes.limits: USD 50,000 is a facilitation quota, not an absolute ceiling for documented outside-individual current income; foreign-PR-card rule applies to the purchase quota.
routes.tax_treatment: Underlying income tax and US income/FX analysis are separate; no universal conversion-tax rate is established.
pros: Direct bank audit trail
Can support genuine income above the facilitation quota
No need to create an artificial asset sale
cons: Document-heavy
Bank classification/acceptance can block execution
Commercial quote still required
routes.flag: User salary provenance, classification, bank and quote are unverified.

routes.name: Existing foreign-currency savings wire after lawful conversion
routes.mechanism: First convert CNY under a lawful basis, then remit foreign currency from the person's FX savings account under the applicable current-account evidence rules.
routes.eligibility: Account holder with lawfully held FX and a genuine permitted outward current-account purpose.
requirements: Authentic transaction evidence where required above the bank-handling threshold
routes.limits: The cited implementation rules distinguish FX-account remittance and hand-held cash thresholds; they are not a new CNY conversion entitlement.
routes.tax_treatment: Moving principal is analyzed separately from underlying income and any currency gain/loss.
pros: Uses ordinary banking rails
Separates conversion from remittance execution
cons: Does not solve an undocumented CNY source
Purpose/evidence and bank controls still apply
routes.flag: No existing FX balance, purpose or bank quote was supplied.

routes.name: Reconvert unused RMB from a prior exchange
routes.mechanism: Use the original exchange memo to reconvert qualifying unused RMB under the outside-individual reconversion rule.
routes.eligibility: Outside individual who previously exchanged foreign currency into RMB and can document it.
requirements: Compliance with the rule's validity and small-value exceptions
routes.limits: Original memo reconversion validity is 24 months under the cited amended rules; small same-day exceptions are stated separately.
routes.tax_treatment: No blanket tax result is inferred; original income and currency basis still matter.
pros: Purpose-built rule for leftover RMB
Avoids treating all CNY as new China income
cons: Only works for documented prior exchange
Not a route for unexplained accumulated savings
routes.flag: Original exchange records are unverified.

routes.name: Lawful cross-border RMB, then convert abroad
routes.mechanism: Bank sends lawful current-account RMB cross-border; a receiving bank or provider converts RMB to USD outside mainland China.
routes.eligibility: Genuine lawful current-account transaction, including qualifying salary, with both banks supporting the corridor.
requirements: Receiving-bank CNY acceptance and conversion service
routes.limits: No universal personal RMB export quota is inferred from the 2020 notice; capital-account transfers are not authorized by this current-account provision.
routes.tax_treatment: China/US income tax does not disappear because conversion occurs later or elsewhere.
pros: May avoid an in-China conversion bottleneck
Keeps a bank record
cons: Two institutions and possibly two cost layers
Offshore RMB rate may differ from onshore CNY
Receiving bank may refuse or restrict CNY
routes.flag: Receiving bank, corridor, rate and fees are unverified.

routes.name: Wise CNY salary transfer
routes.mechanism: Eligible personal customer funds CNY from own China bank/Alipay; Wise's licensed partner and Wise convert/send to an own overseas account or Wise Account.
routes.eligibility: Not mainland Chinese; working or previously worked in China; valid Chinese tax record showing taxes paid within the last three years; personal account.
requirements: Own overseas bank account or supported Wise Account
routes.limits: Bank funding CNY 300,000/transfer; Alipay CNY 50,000/transfer; overall limit generally documented China salary after Chinese tax, non-expiring. First verification 1–2 working days; funding usually 0–1 and conversion up to 2 working days.
routes.tax_treatment: Provider route does not change underlying China/US income tax; documented after-tax salary limit is a sending control, not a tax rate.
pros: Official product-specific outbound-CNY instructions
Own-account audit trail
Published funding caps and process timing
cons: Origin-sensitive eligibility; US citizenship alone is insufficient
Only documented salary scope
Fees require a live quote; unfunded transfers can occupy limit
routes.flag: Do not assume a mainland-origin naturalized US citizen qualifies; user origin, tax records and quote are unverified.

routes.name: Western Union via China partner bank for overseas cash pickup
routes.mechanism: China resident sends through a listed partner bank's online/mobile or branch channel; recipient collects cash abroad.
routes.eligibility: China resident accepted by the partner bank; passport is listed as acceptable ID subject to Chinese banking rules and bank country/passport controls.
requirements: Partner-bank profile/debit card for online route or branch visit
routes.limits: Direct recipient-bank-account delivery is temporarily unavailable. Partner banks and PSBC's country whitelist apply; no China-specific amount/fee quote verified.
routes.tax_treatment: No provider-specific tax exemption; underlying income, currency gain and US cash reporting remain separate.
pros: Official outbound-China product description
Cash-pickup delivery can be fast
Named partner-bank channels
cons: Not a verified direct-to-US-bank route
Cash handling/security and deposit work remain
Bank restrictions can defeat passport acceptance
Fees/limits blank
routes.flag: User residence, bank acceptance, destination and quote are unverified.

routes.name: MoneyGram agent sending from China
routes.mechanism: Generic agent workflow: find location, bring photo ID and funds, answer agent questions.
requirements: Valid photo ID per generic page
Funds and information requested by agent
routes.tax_treatment: No China-specific outbound tax or reporting conclusion can be drawn from the generic page.
pros: Official generic agent instructions exist
cons: China-specific outbound availability, delivery product, passport acceptance, limits and fees not verified
routes.flag: Leave eligibility, limits and costs blank; do not present as an executable route.

routes.name: Remitly outbound from China
routes.tax_treatment: Inbound USD-to-CNY pricing is not evidence for outbound CNY taxation or cost.
pros: Official page verifies sending TO China from the US
cons: Retrieved official product is the opposite direction
No verified outbound-China product or quote
routes.flag: Outbound mechanism, eligibility, limits and costs remain blank/unverified.

routes.name: Genuine business / service-income remittance
routes.mechanism: Remit genuinely earned business/service income with contracts, invoices, tax and transaction evidence through the bank's current-account process.
routes.eligibility: Actual lawful service/business income; not a fabricated consulting contract to move savings.
requirements: Tax filing for outbound service-trade payments above USD 50,000 equivalent unless an exception applies
routes.limits: USD 50,000 is the cited service-trade tax-filing threshold, not a universal transfer ceiling.
routes.tax_treatment: China tax depends on income category/residence; US worldwide income and credit rules still apply.
pros: Matches a genuine income source
Bank documentation supports auditability
cons: Cannot relabel unrelated savings as service income
Tax and contract evidence may be extensive
routes.flag: No business/service facts or quote were supplied.

routes.name: Declared FIE dividend credited to the individual
routes.mechanism: A genuine foreign-invested-enterprise distribution is taxed/withheld under the current individual rule, then any resulting lawful personal RMB is handled under the bank's source-evidence process.
routes.eligibility: Actual individual shareholder receiving a genuine distribution; not a manufactured dividend from unrelated savings.
routes.limits: From 2026-09-01 the individual FIE dividend/bonus IIT rate is 20% under Announcement 2026 No.27; treaty eligibility must be separately established.
routes.tax_treatment: 20% Chinese IIT is on the dividend income, not on the entire pre-existing bank balance. US tax/FTC and treaty analysis remain separate.
pros: Recognizes a genuine income category
Current tax rule is explicitly verified
cons: Creates/recognizes taxable income rather than merely moving principal
Old foreign-individual exemption is obsolete
Bank execution quote still needed
routes.flag: No shareholding, distribution date, treaty residence or quote is established.

routes.name: Property-sale net proceeds
routes.mechanism: Complete a genuine property sale and tax/title process, then remit the permitted net proceeds under the capital-account guidance.
routes.eligibility: Actual qualifying property owner/seller under the applicable outside-person/property rules.
requirements: Reconciliation of sale proceeds, taxes and bank credits
Bank/SAFE process required by the actual status
routes.limits: Remittance limited to sale proceeds less associated taxes under the cited guidance; USD 50,000 filing threshold is not a transfer ceiling.
routes.tax_treatment: China home-sale exemption has its own conditions; US gain/basis and possible main-home exclusion are separate. Do not tax or exempt the whole sale price by assumption.
pros: Purpose-built route for genuine sale proceeds
Net-proceeds rule is documented
cons: Selling an asset solely to move cash adds market/transaction risk
Title/tax consistency can take time
Not a solution for unrelated savings
routes.flag: No property, sale, tax basis or quote was supplied.

routes.name: Immigration-property transfer approval
routes.mechanism: Apply to transfer realized lawful assets owned before obtaining the qualifying foreign/HK/Macao/Taiwan status; after approval the bank remits to the applicant's own overseas account.
routes.eligibility: Defined foreign permanent resident/citizen or HK/Macao/Taiwan resident with qualifying pre-status assets.
routes.limits: 2014 amendment removed staged remittances; above RMB 500,000 follows headquarters review routing. Guide states 20 working days plus possible 10-day extension, no approval fee or numerical quantity limit.
routes.tax_treatment: Approval is not a tax exemption; underlying asset/income tax and US reporting remain separate.
pros: Distinct capital-account route for qualifying pre-status wealth
No obsolete staged schedule
Official no-approval-fee statement
cons: US citizenship alone does not establish eligibility
Acquisition-date and status evidence are restrictive
Bank/document costs are not zero by implication
routes.flag: Status history, acquisition dates, asset records and execution costs are unverified.

routes.name: Inheritance-property transfer approval
routes.mechanism: Qualifying foreign/HK/Macao/Taiwan heir documents inherited mainland property and applies through the designated SAFE/bank process.
routes.eligibility: Actual lawful inheritance and qualifying heir status under the guide.
routes.limits: Separate applications for different decedents; guide states 20 working days plus possible 10-day extension and no administrative approval fee/quantity limit.
routes.tax_treatment: US gift/bequest reporting is distinct from income tax and foreign-trust reporting; China tax depends on the actual inherited assets/income.
pros: Purpose-built inheritance route
Official document checklist
cons: Not available for merely relabelled personal savings
Probate/title/tax evidence can be complex
US Form 3520 may apply to a genuine bequest
routes.flag: No inheritance facts, values or costs were supplied.

routes.name: Foreign-investor equity-sale proceeds
routes.mechanism: A genuine foreign investor's domestic equity disposal is registered and the bank handles the related outward payment under direct-investment controls.
routes.eligibility: Actual foreign investor and genuine equity transaction; not a wrapper created to move unrelated deposits.
requirements: Tax evidence and bank authenticity review
routes.limits: No universal numeric ceiling or current detailed document list is inferred from the amended 2012 notice; its old operational attachments were later repealed.
routes.tax_treatment: China equity-transfer tax and US gain/basis/reporting must be analyzed separately; no rate is assigned to the user.
pros: Recognizes genuine investment-exit proceeds
Bank handling based on registration is supported by official main text
cons: Requires a real investment and transaction
Current detailed checklist/tax calculation remains unverified
Creating a structure can add PFIC/corporation reporting
routes.flag: Investment, transaction, current bank checklist, tax and quote are unverified.

routes.name: Foreign-investor capital reduction / liquidation proceeds
routes.mechanism: After genuine corporate reduction/liquidation and required registration, the bank handles the foreign investor's permitted proceeds.
routes.eligibility: Actual foreign investor entitled to lawful reduction/liquidation proceeds.
routes.limits: No numeric personal quota is inferred; detailed current documents and timing require the applicable current capital-account guide/bank.
routes.tax_treatment: Return of capital, gain and dividend components can differ; no blanket tax-free liquidation claim is made.
pros: Official route for genuine investment exit
Separates corporate proceeds from salary quota
cons: Corporate process can be slow and costly
Not a shortcut for an ordinary CNY savings account
Detailed current checklist unverified
routes.flag: No corporate interest or proceeds are established.

routes.name: Overseas ATM withdrawal with a mainland-issued card
routes.mechanism: Withdraw local cash abroad from the RMB account, then deposit/exchange as needed; this accesses funds rather than wiring USD savings directly.
routes.eligibility: Mainland-issued bank card accepted by the overseas ATM and issuer.
routes.limits: RMB 100,000 per person/year across cards and RMB 10,000 per card/day for overseas cash withdrawal.
routes.tax_treatment: Underlying income and currency basis remain separate; US cash reporting can apply when carrying proceeds into the US.
pros: Useful for limited cash needs
No separate outward-wire application for each ATM withdrawal
cons: Low annual volume
Issuer/ATM fees and FX spread unverified
Cash security/deposit friction
Not a large-balance repatriation solution
routes.flag: Card issuer, destination ATM, fees and user travel are unverified.

routes.name: Overseas card spending
routes.mechanism: Use the China account/card to pay genuine overseas expenses directly.
routes.eligibility: Issuer/card network supports the merchant and transaction.
routes.limits: Ordinary overseas card consumption is not subject to the ATM cash-withdrawal quota; issuer/network limits still apply.
routes.tax_treatment: Spending does not erase underlying income tax; blocked-income deferral, if previously elected, can be affected by personal spending.
pros: Avoids cash withdrawal quota for genuine spending
Useful while travelling
cons: Does not deliver USD savings to a US account
Merchant acceptance, issuer spread and fees unverified
Fake purchases/cash-out schemes are not recommended
routes.flag: Not equivalent to repatriating savings; card terms and expenses are unverified.

routes.name: Carry RMB cash out, then convert in the US
routes.mechanism: Lawfully carry RMB within China's per-person/per-crossing limit and exchange it with a US provider afterward.
routes.eligibility: Traveller complying with China exit and US entry rules.
requirements: RMB cash within the published limit
China Customs declaration process where applicable
US FinCEN 105 if total covered instruments exceed USD 10,000 equivalent
US provider willing to exchange CNY
routes.limits: China limit RMB 20,000 per person per entry/exit under PBOC Announcement 2004 No.18, confirmed in later official guidance; not a USD 50,000 allowance.
routes.tax_treatment: Carrying principal is not a new income-tax calculation by itself; underlying income/FX basis and reporting remain separate.
pros: Simple for a small residual amount
China-side numerical limit verified from primary/official sources
cons: Very low capacity
US CNY exchange spread/availability unverified
Travel/security cost
Do not use repeated crossings to evade controls
routes.flag: Travel plans and US exchange quote are unverified.

routes.name: Convert lawfully in China and carry USD cash with required permits
routes.mechanism: Lawfully purchase/withdraw USD, obtain any required cash-exit permit, carry it and declare correctly on US entry.
routes.eligibility: Lawful conversion basis and traveller meeting cash withdrawal/exit rules.
requirements: Bank withdrawal review; special prior SAFE filing above the stated withdrawal threshold
Bank or SAFE foreign-cash carrying permit where required
routes.limits: No prior-entry record: up to USD 5,000 equivalent no permit; above 5,000 through 10,000 bank permit; above 10,000 SAFE permit and in-principle restriction/special cases. Frequent-traveler rules are stricter. Withdrawal up to USD 10,000/day at bank; above that only the stated special-destination filing process.
routes.tax_treatment: No cash-route tax exemption; underlying income and currency gain/loss remain separate.
pros: Published permit tiers resolve the earlier cash-rule evidence gap
Can work for genuine travel cash needs
cons: Not a scalable large-balance solution
Multiple controls and physical risk
US declaration is not China exit permission
Do not split among companions to evade rules
routes.flag: Prior-entry declaration, travel frequency, special-case eligibility and costs are unverified.

routes.name: Bank draft or traveler's cheque
routes.mechanism: Official cash rules mention carrying foreign-currency drafts/traveler's checks as alternatives to physical cash, but a current issuing bank and acceptance network were not verified.
requirements: Issuer and beneficiary requirements would need confirmation
routes.tax_treatment: Underlying income/FX and US monetary-instrument reporting rules still need application to the actual instrument.
pros: Recognized historically as a non-cash instrument option
cons: Current product availability, issuance, acceptance, loss replacement and fees unverified
routes.flag: Do not present as currently executable without issuer/acceptance evidence.

routes.name: QDII / authorized overseas investment program
routes.mechanism: Invest through a qualified domestic institution under the authorized investment regime.
routes.eligibility: Actual program/investor eligibility and investment rules.
routes.limits: No free personal withdrawal quota is created by the investment program.
routes.tax_treatment: Investment income/gains and US PFIC/entity reporting can apply; not a tax-free conversion method.
pros: Lawful investment channel where genuinely available
cons: Adds market/product risk
Does not establish a right to keep or withdraw proceeds abroad
Not a solution for moving existing savings
routes.flag: No product, eligibility, redemption/repatriation terms or quote verified.

routes.name: Registered employer overseas-listed-company equity plan
routes.mechanism: A genuine registered plan uses a domestic agency and dedicated accounts for permitted payments and return of proceeds.
routes.eligibility: Actual participant in a qualifying registered employer plan.
requirements: Dedicated account and approved payment quota
routes.limits: Official Beijing guide says investment principal and realized proceeds sent abroad should generally return to China within six months of realization; later proceeds may be retained in a domestic FX account or settled.
routes.tax_treatment: Equity compensation/investment tax and US reporting remain separate.
pros: Lawful channel for a genuine existing plan
cons: Proceeds-return rule makes it non-equivalent to permanent repatriation
Cannot be invented for unrelated CNY savings
routes.flag: No employer plan is established; do not create one as a workaround.

routes.name: Open an offshore bank account
routes.mechanism: Opening an account abroad creates a destination, not permission to transfer CNY out of China.
routes.eligibility: Receiving bank's own KYC/residence rules; China outward-transfer rules separately.
requirements: Lawful China-side transfer basis and evidence
routes.limits: No China transfer entitlement arises from account opening.
routes.tax_treatment: New foreign accounts can add FBAR/FATCA reporting; they do not erase income tax.
pros: May provide a legitimate destination for an already lawful transfer
cons: Does not solve the China-side bottleneck
Additional account/reporting obligations
routes.flag: Receiving-bank acceptance and China-side basis are unverified.

routes.name: Buy an insurance policy / later surrender abroad
routes.mechanism: Insurance payments/benefits have their own rules; buying a policy is not a documented right to repatriate the premium as savings.
requirements: Actual lawful product and benefit terms would be required
routes.tax_treatment: Policy income/surrender and US foreign-asset/PFIC/trust issues can be complex; no tax-free result is inferred.
pros: Genuine insurance can serve a genuine protection need
cons: No verified outbound surrender/repatriation product
Surrender charges, market risk and tax/reporting complexity
Not recommended as a money-transfer workaround
routes.flag: Product, benefit, surrender and cross-border payment terms are blank/unverified.

routes.name: Crypto / stablecoin bridge (CNY → USDT → USD)
routes.mechanism: Using virtual currency/exchanges or P2P settlement to bypass banking controls.
routes.tax_treatment: US digital-asset income/transaction reporting can still apply; illegality in China is not cured by US tax reporting.
cons: 2021 official notice treats virtual-currency-related financial activity as illegal
Overseas exchanges serving mainland residents over the internet are addressed as illegal financial activity
Counterparty, freeze and enforcement risk
routes.flag: Rejected as a repatriation strategy.

routes.name: Underground bank / private P2P settlement
routes.mechanism: Pay CNY domestically to a broker who pays USD abroad outside authorized FX channels.
routes.tax_treatment: No tax shortcut; illegal FX trading and transfer penalties remain possible.
cons: Unauthorized FX settlement
Counterparty/fraud/freeze risk
No reliable lawful audit trail
routes.flag: Rejected; advertised rates are not verified or recommended.

routes.name: Quota splitting through relatives, friends or multiple accounts
routes.mechanism: Divide one person's transfer among other people/accounts/cards to evade facilitation or reporting controls.
routes.tax_treatment: Splitting does not change underlying income tax or US reporting duties.
cons: Explicit anti-splitting controls
Potential FX penalties
US family/group cash aggregation and account reporting defeat the intended disguise
routes.flag: Rejected; genuine separate gifts/transfers require their own facts and are not assumed.

routes.name: Fabricated salary, trade, property sale or dividend
routes.mechanism: Create false contracts, invoices, distributions or asset transactions to justify conversion/remittance.
routes.tax_treatment: A fabricated label can create additional tax/false-document exposure rather than reduce tax.
cons: Fraudulent conversion/illegal transfer risk
Bank authenticity checks
Potential administrative/criminal consequences
routes.flag: Rejected.

routes.name: Relabel own savings as a foreign gift or trust distribution
routes.mechanism: Route own money through another person/entity and call it a gift, inheritance or trust distribution.
routes.tax_treatment: US gift/bequest and trust rules depend on the real legal relationship; Form 3520 thresholds are not a tax-free transfer allowance.
cons: Misstates ownership/source
Can add foreign-trust/entity reporting and penalties
Does not establish China-side permission
routes.flag: Rejected as a disguise; genuine gifts/inheritances are separately listed only where facts support them.
